messages:
emily_g: FYI hitting a weird bundling regression when customers import the Node TS SDK in Next.js + webpack app. getting ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED in prod :/
emily_g: repro steps: ts-sdk@2.3.1, next 12, webpack 5, app built with pnpm
emily_g: error from server when calling our hosted endpoint (customer) is a 401, but when I reproduce locally without bundling it's fine. suspect bundler stripping auth header or changing import path.
raj_s: can you paste package.json from the published package and the bundle output?
emily_g: paste below — published package.json exports section:```json
{"name":"@redwood/sdk","version":"2.3.1","main":"dist/index.cjs.js","module":"dist/index.esm.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"./package.json":"./package.json","./*":{"import":"./dist/*.mjs","require":"./dist/*.cjs"}},"files":["dist"]}```
emily_g: webpack build output shows warnings: WARN Module not found: Error: Package path ./dist/index.mjs is not exported by package @redwood/sdk
nate_ops: that exports map looks non-standard — using globs in exports is tricky for node resolver. also note we publish .mjs vs .esm — but your exports import path points to a glob. some bundlers (terser/webpack) can't resolve it.
olivia_repro: i reproduced locally with a simple webpack app. got runtime: TypeError: (0 , _redwood.default) is not a function after build. dev import works.
raj_s: two likely issues: 1) conditional exports/globs causing bundler resolution to pick the wrong entry (maybe CJS stub that lacks default export). 2) Next's webpack tree shaking + minifier rewriting ESM->CJS interop. can you try changing exports to explicit subpaths instead of globs?
emily_g: tried replacing exports with explicit entries:```json
{"exports":{"./index":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"},"./utils":{"import":"./dist/utils.mjs","require":"./dist/utils.cjs"}}}```
emily_g: rebuilt, republished to staging. still seeing 401s for customer's prod build. local repro still fine.
emily_g: on the prod bundle I inspected network tab and the Authorization header is missing from fetch to api.redwood.com
emate_ops: could the fetch polyfill/whatwg-fetch used by next be stripping credentials? or is axios instance created in package relying on global fetch that bundler replaced?
omelia: (support-bot) FYI: recent change #543 added code that reads token from process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY when global fetch is undefined.
raj_s: check whether bundler is replacing process.env.* at build time (webpack DefinePlugin). If package code expects runtime process.env it may be compiled away in user's build.
emily_g: aha — the SDK code does: const KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || globalThis.__REDWOOD__?.apiKey; then uses KEY to set header. with webpack DefinePlugin commonly injecting string values, some apps set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY="" in their build so it ends up empty.
emily_g: customer app uses next.config.js env: REDWOOD_API_KEY="" (they thought empty value means runtime).
raj_s: that explains missing header. still need to fix packaging to avoid export/interop break though. two action items: 1) patch SDK to prefer runtime-injectable global (window.__REDWOOD__) before process.env, and document that process.env is baked at build time. 2) simplify exports to explicit files to avoid resolver issues.
nate_ops: for quick mitigation, we can backfill a minor release that keeps cjs default export compatibility: add `module.exports = require('./dist/index.cjs')` and set `exports: {".":{"require":"./dist/index.cjs","import":"./dist/index.mjs"}}` and include a rollup of ESM->CJS interop wrapper.
emily_g: i'm going to create a reproducible minimal repo and post link. olivia_repro — can you try reproducing with that change?
olivia_repro: will do. quick question — do we include a note in support reply about how bundlers can bake env vars and strip headers?
raj_s: yes include steps: ask for their package.json, next.config.js, webpack define plugin usage, and whether they use `next export` or serverless. also ask for build artifact (the bundled file) so we can search for Authorization string.
emily_g: thanks. opening a follow-up ticket to patch SDK and publish 2.3.2 with explicit exports + runtime-global-first auth fallback. adding repro repo and minimal webpack example to ticket. :thumbsup:
